chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, raised it (to the Imam).
Regarding the Words of the Mighty and Majestic: 'So whoever does not find (an animal) should fast for three days during the Hajj and seven when he returns; these ten are complete.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'Its completion is the completion of the sacrificial animal.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for fasting when one cannot afford the Hajj sacrifice?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the ten-day fasting expiation (three during Hajj, seven upon return) serves as a complete substitute for the sacrificial animal (udhiyah) when a pilgrim cannot afford it. Scholars emphasize that this ruling underscores the flexibility in Hajj rituals, ensuring that financial inability does not invalidate the pilgrimage's completeness, provided the prescribed fasts are fulfilled with sincerity.
